full_judgment: 6. It appears that the trial Court on elaborate discussion of the evidence on record, both oral and documentary, came to the specific finding that the plaintiffs proved their title in respect of 84 decimals of land only though they claimed their title in 2.18 acres land and on such finding decreed the suit declaring plaintiffs title in respect of the said area of the land and also passed a decree in preliminary form for the same area of the land. The Appellate Court being the last Court of fact without discussing the evidence on record and adverting the findings of the trial Court allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit, one of the reasons assigned by the Appellate Court in setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court is that it did not mention any specific plot number and that the chouhaddis of the suit land given by PWs 2 and 3 were not at all consistent (সংগত পূর্ণ নয়), so possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land was not proved beyond reasonable doubt (in the judgment in Bangla it has recorded as "সন্দেহাতীত ভাবে প্রমাণিত হয় না" completely forgetting that the suit was for declaration of title and for partition as well. The High Court Division though found that "on reading the said judgment I find that the same cannot be treated as judgment of reversal as per the provision of law provided in the Code of Civil Procedure. The defendants did not deny the entire claim of the plaintiffs as they claimed by way of settlement and successive transfer, but the Appellate Court without considering the documents of title of the plaintiffs dismissed the suit as a whole, meaning that the plaintiffs have no right, title and possession in any part of the suit land. The basis of such judgment is nothing but that the Assistant Judge decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs in respect of only 0.84 acre of land without mentioning any plot number or khatian number. But finding of the learned Additional District fudge is apparently illegal because the learned Assistant Judge arrived into his decision on consideration and discussion of the materials on record and the suit was not decreed finally. The suit as being a suit of partition as well as for declaration of title was decreed preliminarily and to make it as final the Advocate Commissioner should specify shares of the plaintiffs or it may be specified amicably between the parties before drawing up the final decree. Before drawing up the final decree, finding of the learned Additional District judge is not sustainable without considering the evidence on record and see whether the trial Court was justified in decreeing the suit in the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record made the Rule absolute just restoring those of the trial Court.
